content: This schedule outlines vaccination recommendations effective as of January 1, 2017. Any missed doses should be administered at a subsequent visit when appropriate and feasible. Combination vaccines are generally preferred over separate injections of equivalent component vaccines. Suspected cases of vaccine-preventable diseases must be reported to the state or local health department. These recommendations should be read alongside the accompanying footnotes. For individuals who are behind on vaccinations or starting late, catch-up vaccinations should be provided at the earliest opportunity, as indicated by the green bars in the schedule. To determine the minimum intervals between doses, refer to the catch-up schedule. School entry and adolescent vaccine age groups are shaded in gray. For catch-up immunization schedules for individuals aged 4 months through 18 years who are late or more than one month behind, the vaccine series does not need to be restarted regardless of the time elapsed between doses. Use the section appropriate for the child’s age and always refer to the footnotes. For calculating intervals between doses, 4 weeks equals 28 days, and intervals of 4 months or greater are determined by calendar months. Vaccine doses administered 4 days or fewer before the minimum interval are considered valid. Doses given 5 or more days earlier than the minimum interval or age should not be counted as valid and must be repeated with the recommended minimum interval. Hepatitis B (HepB) Vaccine: Administer a monovalent HepB vaccine to all newborns within 24 hours of birth. For infants born to HBsAg-positive mothers, administer 0.5 mL of hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG) within 12 hours of birth. These infants should be tested for HBsAg and anti-HBs at 9–12 months of age or 1–2 months after completing the HepB series if delayed. If the mother’s HBsAg status is unknown, administer the HepB vaccine within 12 hours of birth regardless of birth weight. For infants weighing less than 2,000 grams, also administer HBIG within 12 hours of birth. Determine the mother’s HBsAg status as soon as possible. If the mother is HBsAg-positive, administer HBIG to infants weighing 2,000 grams or more within 7 days of birth. The second dose should be administered at 1–2 months of age. Monovalent HepB vaccine should be used for doses before 6 weeks of age. Infants who did not receive a birth dose should receive 3 doses of a HepB-containing vaccine on a schedule of 0, 1–2 months, and 6 months. The third dose should be administered at least 8 weeks after the second dose and at least 16 weeks after the first dose. The final dose should not be given earlier than 24 weeks of age. A total of 4 doses is permitted when a combination vaccine containing HepB is used after the birth dose. Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR) Vaccine: Administer a 2-dose series of MMR vaccine at 12–15 months and 4–6 years of age. The second dose may be given earlier if at least 4 weeks have passed since the first dose. For international travel, administer 1 dose of MMR vaccine to infants aged 6–11 months. These children should be revaccinated with 2 doses of MMR vaccine, the first at 12–15 months and the second at least 4 weeks later. Ensure all school-aged children and adolescents have received 2 doses of MMR vaccine, with a minimum interval of 4 weeks between doses. Varicella (VAR) Vaccine: Administer a 2-dose series of VAR vaccine at 12–15 months and 4–6 years of age. The second dose may be given earlier if at least 3 months have passed since the first dose. If the second dose was administered at least 4 weeks after the first dose, it is valid. For children aged 7–12 years, the minimum interval between doses is 3 months. For individuals aged 13 years and older, the minimum interval is 4 weeks. Meningococcal Vaccines: For children with anatomic or functional asplenia or HIV infection, administer 2 primary doses of MenACWY vaccine at least 8 weeks apart. Do not administer MenACWY until 2 years of age and at least 4 weeks after completing all PCV13 doses. For children with persistent complement component deficiency, administer 2 primary doses of MenACWY vaccine at least 12 weeks apart for those aged 9–23 months and at least 8 weeks apart for those aged 24 months and older. For individuals aged 10 years or older, administer a 2-dose series of MenB vaccine (Bexsero) with doses at least 1 month apart or a 3-dose series of MenB vaccine (Trumenba) with the second dose 1–2 months after the first and the third dose at least 6 months after the first. The two MenB vaccines are not interchangeable; the same product must be used for all doses. Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccine: Administer a 2-dose series of HPV vaccine at 0 and 6–12 months to adolescents aged 11–12 years. The series can start at age 9 years. For individuals initiating vaccination before age 15, the recommended schedule is 2 doses at 0 and 6–12 months. For those starting at age 15 or older, the schedule is 3 doses at 0, 1–2, and 6 months. In a 2-dose schedule, the minimum interval is 5 months between the first and second dose. In a 3-dose schedule, the minimum intervals are 4 weeks between the first and second dose, 12 weeks between the second and third dose, and 5 months between the first and third dose. HPV vaccination is not recommended during pregnancy. If a woman becomes pregnant after starting the series, delay the remaining doses until after pregnancy. These guidelines are designed to ensure timely and effective immunization for all individuals, with specific recommendations for catch-up schedules and special populations.
